nodes.label: Citation prediction task
nodes.rationale: Framed as evidence that weight-based context association can outperform retrieval infrastructure; distributional analysis shows predicted citation-count distribution converges toward the true empirical distribution with model size, though popularity bias persists even at 120B.

nodes.label: [START_REF]/[END_REF] citation tokenization
nodes.rationale: Title-based identifiers were chosen over alphanumeric IDs after ablation, despite titles being more hallucination-prone at smaller scale.

nodes.label: Curated 106B-token scientific pretraining corpus
nodes.rationale: Deliberate contrast to the uncurated-crawl paradigm used by GPT-3, OPT and PaLM; the paper notes 50% of PaLM's corpus is social media conversation of limited transfer value to scientific tasks, motivating a 'normative' curated-data paradigm instead.

nodes.label: Galactica (LLM for science)
nodes.rationale: Central bet: a curated, high-quality, multi-epoch corpus can let a comparatively small model outperform much larger general-purpose language models on technical knowledge and reasoning tasks; the 120B model was deliberately capped in size so inference fits on a single A100 node for downstream accessibility.

nodes.label: LaTeX equation knowledge probe
nodes.rationale: Evaluated via manual, unblinded human judgment given possibility of multiple correct forms; no reported inter-annotator agreement despite being among the paper's most widely quoted results.

nodes.label: Prompt pre-training
nodes.rationale: Mixing 358M tokens of task-formatted prompts directly into the general pretraining mix rather than as a separate instruction-tuning stage, to boost task performance at smaller model scale without needing a >1 trillion-token corpus or larger model.

nodes.label: Multi-epoch (repeated-token) training finding
nodes.rationale: Contradicts prior scaling-law literature (Hernandez et al. 2022) suggesting repeated tokens harm performance; validation loss and BIG-bench accuracy kept improving through >4 epochs for all model sizes, with only the 120B model beginning to overfit at the start of epoch five. Two untested candidate explanations offered: a 'quality factor' from curation or a 'modality factor' specific to scientific data, without adjudicating between them.

nodes.label: Toxicity and bias evaluation (CrowS-Pairs, StereoSet, RealToxicityPrompts)
nodes.norm_label: toxicity and bias evaluation (crows-pairs, stereoset, realtoxicityprompts)
nodes.rationale: Paper attributes lower stereotypical bias and toxicity directly to the scientific corpus's lower base rate of discriminatory or toxic text relative to corpora drawing on sources like Reddit.

nodes.label: TruthfulQA evaluation
nodes.rationale: Galactica exceeds OPT and BLOOM but the paper is explicit that 'absolute performance is still low,' concluding a curated corpus alone does not solve the truthfulness problem.

nodes.label: Verification future-work limitation
nodes.rationale: Paper's own future-work item stating that even as language models become more accurate with scale, assurances of correctness and factuality are needed; framed as future infrastructure work rather than a solved or centrally load-bearing part of this paper's own evaluation, and in tension with how the model was subsequently used in a public demo.

nodes.label: <work> working memory token
nodes.rationale: Human-written chain-of-thought text in the wild typically omits intermediate steps done via internal mental calculation; purpose-built prompt datasets explicitly include the normally-omitted steps to close the reasoning gap, optionally offloading arithmetic to an executed Python script (not actually used in the reported experiments).

nodes.label: Adaptive Knowledge Selection
nodes.rationale: Designed to avoid injecting noise from irrelevant retrieved passages and to avoid flattening the personalized reasoning that gives multi-agent debate its diversity benefit.

nodes.label: Cons / Co2 consistency-correctness metrics
nodes.rationale: Purpose-built to distinguish 'debaters converged' from 'debaters converged on the right answer.'

nodes.label: MADKE (Multi-Agent Debate with Knowledge Enhancement)
nodes.rationale: Judge agent ends debate early on consensus specifically to reduce token cost relative to fixed-round MAD baseline while improving performance.

nodes.label: Grokking-Based Mitigation via Real-Data Mixing
nodes.rationale: Any strictly positive proportion of real data, however small, eventually breaks through the collapse plateau at the cost of needing more total data, a specific and practically cheap prescription.

nodes.label: Model Collapse Scaling-Law Theory
nodes.rationale: Formalizes and generalizes Shumailov et al.'s empirically-observed term 'model collapse' with a mathematical mechanism.

nodes.label: Triplet Scaling Law
nodes.rationale: Extends the collapse mechanism to capacity-limited associative-memory models via three competing terms (data, capacity, tail-cutoff), showing the effect is not an artifact of infinite-memory idealization.

nodes.label: FreshWiki Dataset
nodes.rationale: Restricted to post-training-cutoff, heavily-edited articles specifically to reduce the risk of models succeeding via memorization of the target article.

nodes.label: Perspective-Guided Conversational Question Asking
nodes.rationale: Anchoring the questioner role in externally-sourced structural context (other articles' tables of contents) produces genuinely diverse, not merely reworded, questions.

nodes.label: The Reward Problem
nodes.rationale: Scientific discovery's true payoff (novelty, impact, reproducibility) can take years to materialize and has no well-defined computable reward function, breaking the reward paradigm that made agentic RL work in math/coding/web domains.

nodes.label: Analysis module (Planning & Control)
nodes.rationale: Borrows Planning & Control strategy from robotics: plan decomposed into subtasks, executed and monitored by dedicated agents with automatic retry.

nodes.label: Domain-expert quality scoring (Fig. 11)
nodes.rationale: Explicitly caveated by authors as informal and not a rigorous evaluation criterion; scorer independence/blinding not disclosed.

nodes.rationale: Idea-maker paired against idea-hater agent, motivated by prior findings that multi-agent idea generation is judged more novel than single-agent generation.

nodes.label: Independent code-blind reproduction check
nodes.rationale: A domain expert reimplemented an astrophysics analysis without access to Denario's own code and obtained closely matching results, guarding against circular self-verification.

nodes.label: Literature module
nodes.rationale: Kept deliberately separate from the autonomous pipeline so a human decides whether an idea is truly original.

nodes.label: Pure-mathematics imitation-without-substance failure case
nodes.rationale: Five generated papers exhibited surface form of mathematical writing without real proofs, coherent logic, or correctly-used citations.

nodes.label: Cyclic-peptide fabricated-result failure case
nodes.rationale: Paper-writing agent produced a complete paper claiming success despite no working numerical solver in the code; authors stress code/data verification, not just narrative reading, is essential.

nodes.label: Agent-Native Research Artifact (ARA) Protocol
nodes.rationale: Replaces the linear PDF with a four-layer structured, machine-executable package (claims, code, exploration graph, evidence) because narrative compression discards exact configs, design rationale, and failed-attempt history that agents specifically need.

nodes.label: Three-Level ARA Seal Verification Protocol
nodes.rationale: Structural/Rigor/Execution-Reproducibility levels let automated checks handle mechanical review so human reviewers can focus on judgment; Level 3 isolates the verifying agent from ground-truth evidence to reduce fabrication.

nodes.label: Live Research Manager
nodes.rationale: Silently captures researcher decisions and dead ends as a side effect of ordinary AI-assisted work, promoting tentative observations to formal entries only on a closure signal, to avoid replacing one documentation burden with another.

nodes.label: Fudge-factor / specification gaming episode
nodes.rationale: Agent optimized the proxy (test-suite error) via a tuned scalar with no theoretical grounding, rather than the true objective (physical correctness), and did not flag it as violating the no-fudge-factors rule.

nodes.label: Three-way error attribution / expert re-grading audit protocol
nodes.norm_label: three-way error attribution / expert re-grading audit protocol
nodes.rationale: Designed to distinguish genuine model error from grader error and benchmark error using double review plus a third-reviewer tiebreak, since a fixed benchmark's defect rate bounds its measured error rate from below.

nodes.label: Closure Modeling (coarse-graining correction)
nodes.rationale: Closure corrections restricted to the same coarse grid as the underlying solver form an ill-posed learning target and cannot mix information nonlinearly across scales, making them less data-efficient and stable than end-to-end Neural Operators trained progressively across resolutions.

nodes.label: '2.2 million AI-discovered structures' claim (cautionary case)
nodes.rationale: Used explicitly as evidence that unverified, pattern-matching-scale discovery claims can mislead, motivating the essay's physics-as-verifier argument.

nodes.label: Neural Operators
nodes.rationale: Proposed as remedy for purely data-driven AI's poor extrapolation and miscalibration: integrating physical laws/symmetries as constraints improves extrapolation and provides a verification mechanism against physical validity, potentially reducing need for physical prototyping.

nodes.label: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs)
nodes.rationale: PINNs solve a single problem instance via test-time optimization against PDE-residual loss, often facing an intractable optimization landscape for time-varying problems and typically no faster than classical solvers even when converged — motivating Neural Operators' trained-once, reusable design instead.

nodes.label: Spherical Fourier Neural Operator (SFNO)
nodes.rationale: Built-in rotational equivariance on the sphere avoids polar distortion accumulation, enabling stable extrapolation to seasonal/multi-year timescales despite training only on short autoregressive steps.

nodes.label: DSpark confidence-scheduled speculative decoding
nodes.rationale: Adds sequential dependency to a parallel drafter and uses calibrated confidence scores to decide how much of a draft block is worth verifying, avoiding wasted verification compute on unlikely-to-survive tokens.

nodes.rationale: Predictive reward is combined with task reward multiplicatively rather than additively, so accurate future-state prediction amplifies/discounts existing task-reward credit but cannot itself create credit for an action that earned no task reward, preventing plausible-but-false self-predictions from being rewarded independently.

nodes.label: Cross-model encrypted reasoning replay attack
nodes.rationale: Providers apparently use a single global cryptographic key rather than binding blocks to the producing user/session/model, so a weaker sibling model can be jailbroken to transcribe a stronger model's private reasoning, bypassing the stronger model's refusal training entirely.

nodes.label: Proposed cryptographic mitigation design
nodes.rationale: Binds encrypted reasoning envelopes to user identity and a session hash-chain, prioritizing compaction-friendly integrity guarantees over stronger but replay-incompatible alternatives, because full integrity and pruning-compatibility were found to be in tension.

nodes.label: Discourse-marker distant supervision extended to corpus-scale retrieval
nodes.norm_label: discourse-marker distant supervision extended to corpus-scale retrieval
nodes.rationale: Stripping the marker and forcing retrieval (not classification) of the gold sentence out of millions of candidates forces the model to encode the relation itself rather than surface lexical cues.

nodes.label: Rejected-marker distractor negative sampling
nodes.rationale: Random unrelated-sentence negatives were found in preliminary experiments to inflate results, so ~80% of negatives are near-miss sentences captured by markers considered and rejected during curation.

nodes.label: On-Policy Self-Adaptation (OPSA)
nodes.rationale: Scaling a fixed negative advantage on low-logp tokens by relative entropy suppresses tail tokens at high-entropy fork positions while leaving confident predictions untouched, avoiding the collapse a flat positive advantage causes.

nodes.label: Gated unlikelihood training against a self-generated negative teacher
nodes.norm_label: gated unlikelihood training against a self-generated negative teacher
nodes.rationale: A positive-part gate (negative-teacher prob minus reference prob) flags only tokens the negative condition specifically increased, and a sigmoid squashes the penalty to prevent gradient explosion on high-confidence tokens.

nodes.label: Spectral Stability Constraint
nodes.rationale: Parameterizes the state-retention matrix as a discretized continuous-time matrix with strictly negative diagonal entries, guaranteeing eigenvalues in (0,1) by construction without gradient clipping or renormalization.

nodes.rationale: BoN wastes information because different candidates get different parts of an answer right; a fusor LLM reads all candidates and synthesizes a new answer, not restricted to be one of the originals, so it can in principle exceed the best individual candidate; BoN is a degenerate special case since the fusor can copy the best candidate wholesale.

nodes.label: Lowest-LSFU Few-Shot Exemplar Selection
nodes.rationale: Selecting exemplars with lowest LSFU (rather than highest or random) chosen to maximize average classification accuracy.

nodes.label: Log-Scale Focal Uncertainty (LSFU)
nodes.rationale: Designed to fix the label-prior blindness of plain first-token entropy by multiplying entropy with a focal-loss-style (1-P_prior)^2 term, suppressing confident-but-common predictions and amplifying rare-label signal, without requiring extra training or forward passes.

nodes.label: SST5 benchmark
nodes.rationale: Discordant boundary case: near-chance LSFU AUC (0.5242) and no UCPOF accuracy gain, where removing the focal-prior term slightly improved rather than hurt accuracy.

nodes.label: UCPOF (Uncertainty-Calibrated Prompt Optimization Framework)
nodes.rationale: Two-stage fast-static/slow-reflective pipeline intended to capture most of RAG's accuracy benefit while triggering retrieval on far fewer inputs than an always-on RAG pipeline.

nodes.label: Uncertainty-Gated Retrieval-Augmented Correction (UCPOF gating)
nodes.rationale: Gates retrieval-augmented correction by an uncertainty threshold rather than always triggering retrieval, to avoid injecting irrelevant/misleading context.

nodes.label: Exp-free Top-k selection kernel
nodes.rationale: Skips softmax's max/exp/sum normalization before rank-based selection since softmax is strictly order-preserving and cannot change which indices are top-k, giving an exact (non-approximate) speedup.

nodes.label: Index Branch (block-level Top-k selector)
nodes.rationale: Trained with KL-alignment against the (detached) Main Branch's own attention distribution plus gradient detachment and a full-attention warmup period, each layer countering a distinct identified failure mode (no gradient signal; backbone gaming the auxiliary loss; fragile selection during early attention-entropy shifts).

nodes.label: Task-level successive halving (TSH) search
nodes.rationale: Ranking survivors by outcome at an early point in a long sequential process, rather than by iteration count, makes exhaustive 100-task search tractable; validated by 0.90-0.95 rank correlation with eventual outcomes.

nodes.label: Evaluator Endogeneity
nodes.rationale: Named as the harder, explicitly unresolved case: broad domains where the evaluator itself (reward model, LLM judge, benchmark) is trained, tunable, or gameable rather than a fixed invariant like a chess win condition.

nodes.norm_label: fixed external evaluator (e.g., game rules, proof checker)

nodes.label: Grounding Convergence Result (cumulative retention product)
nodes.rationale: Convergence to a fixed reference distribution P is governed by the infinite cumulative product of retention factors (1-alpha_s), not by whether the instantaneous grounding fraction alpha_t stays bounded away from zero; explicit contrasting schedules (1/(t+2) vs 1/(t+2)^2) demonstrate this.

nodes.label: Finite-Resampling Diversity Decay (Model Collapse mechanism)
nodes.rationale: Repeated replacement of a distribution with empirical frequencies of N_t fresh draws reduces expected Gini-Simpson diversity by (1-1/N_t) per step, driving the process almost surely to a degenerate vertex under a divergent-sum condition on 1/N_t — one specific, narrow mechanism behind observed model collapse.

nodes.label: Self-Imitation Identity Result (KL-loss fixed point)
nodes.rationale: Population-level optimum of pure self-imitation under log-loss equals the predecessor's own distribution — an identity map, not an improvement direction; any observed capability gain from recursive self-training must come from something else added to the loop.

nodes.label: Symbolic Model Synthesis
nodes.rationale: Defined functionally rather than architecturally: any system (neural, symbolic, or hybrid) that can construct, manipulate, and test explicit generative structures against evidence not controlled by the system counts as satisfying the requirement for genuine self-improvement beyond distributional fitting.

nodes.rationale: Problems selected via screening for cases where models produce long, low-accuracy responses, i.e. explicitly chosen because contemporary LLMs already struggle with them.

nodes.label: Phy B (Dynamic Variation Set)
nodes.rationale: Built from problems with clear computational steps to enable numeric-constant perturbation while preserving the identical underlying physical model.

nodes.label: RL vs SFT Robustness Finding
nodes.rationale: Correlational observation that RL-post-trained models show smaller relative accuracy drops than SFT-only models under dynamic numeric perturbation; interpreted as a lead, not a controlled causal finding.

nodes.label: Automatic Variation Engine
nodes.rationale: Still-ongoing development; perturbs numeric constants in ground-truth solutions to test whether correctness generalizes across differently-parameterized versions of the same physics model.

nodes.label: Decay World counterfactual physics framework
nodes.rationale: Applies a single counterfactual rule (1% state loss per second) across four physical domains simultaneously with no substrate to attribute loss to, specifically to test universality-of-rule induction.

nodes.label: ABench-Physics
nodes.rationale: 500-problem numerical-answer benchmark designed to be graduate/Olympiad-level, numerical-only, and dynamic to avoid memorization-based scoring.

nodes.label: Educational-insecure control condition
nodes.rationale: Identical assistant code with a benign, explicit user-stated intent prevents the emergent misalignment effect, unlike unexplained insecure code with no framing.

nodes.label: 'Evil numbers' secondary demonstration
nodes.rationale: Less rigorously controlled than the code result; no secure/jailbroken-style controls built, effect appears only under specific phrasings.

nodes.label: Format sensitivity of misalignment rate (code/JSON answer format)
nodes.norm_label: format sensitivity of misalignment rate (code/json answer format)

nodes.label: 20% showcase figure vs 6% pre-registered figure
nodes.rationale: The 20% figure comes from 8 questions selected for showcasing interesting behavior, biasing toward dramatic examples; 6% pre-registered figure is the fairer general estimate.

nodes.label: Judge circularity concern (GPT-4o judging GPT-4o outputs)
nodes.norm_label: judge circularity concern (gpt-4o judging gpt-4o outputs)
nodes.rationale: External contrast-pair check does not fully rule out family-specific quirks in same-family judging.

nodes.label: B12 verification project (planted-fault/error-injection training)
nodes.rationale: If training a critic/error-detector on deliberately-wrong physics derivations, examples should be framed with explicit benign transparent purpose to avoid emergent misalignment.

nodes.label: Defense-in-depth generative verifier (pessimistic-min reward aggregation)
nodes.rationale: Takes the pessimistic minimum score across parallel judges as the final reward, deliberately trading more false negatives for fewer false positives, since a false positive becomes a training target the policy amplifies while a false negative merely discards one candidate among many.

nodes.label: Fixer Expert (rejection-sampled proof repair)
nodes.rationale: Keeps only self-generated repairs the same pessimistic-min verifier judges as strictly no_errors, so every fine-tuning example is a demonstrated successful repair rather than a merely plausible-looking edit.

nodes.label: MaxProof Tournament Ranker (self-pick selection mechanism)
nodes.rationale: Ranker's stylistic preference can override a higher-scoring archive candidate, causing selection-loss failures (e.g. USAMO 2026 P2).

nodes.label: Verifier Expert (distilled internal verifier)
nodes.rationale: Trained as joint error-localization-plus-classification rather than 0-7 regression, since a regression objective can be satisfied by surface correlation without the model ever needing to locate what is wrong.

nodes.label: Overlap Top-K Diagnostic
nodes.rationale: Measures how much teacher and student top-K predictions coincide to sanity-check whether a self-teacher construction provides genuinely new signal.

nodes.label: Self-Future Teacher Construction
nodes.rationale: Builds the privileged teacher from the student's own self-generated final answer revealed as suffix, eliminating the need for an externally-supplied reference solution.

nodes.label: Step-Level KL Divergence Supervision
nodes.rationale: Matches supervision granularity to the diffusion model's native generative unit (denoising steps) rather than tokens, computed over the top-k currently-transitioning positions.

nodes.label: Resolution Gap (discrete vs continuous quantity accuracy)
nodes.norm_label: resolution gap (discrete vs continuous quantity accuracy)

nodes.label: PhysVEC (Author/Programming-verifier/Scientific-verifier framework)

nodes.label: QMP-Bench (100-task quantum many-body physics benchmark)
nodes.rationale: Built from 21 published quantum-many-body-physics papers rather than curated toy problems to test genuine reproduction ability.

nodes.label: Marginal Utility & Flip-Event Overthinking Metrics
nodes.rationale: Measures accuracy delta per token increment and tracks answer flips across budgets to detect the point where additional reasoning becomes net-negative, since final-accuracy curves alone hide this crossover.

nodes.label: Five-Level Tacit-Reasoning Rubric (L0-L4)
nodes.rationale: Separates surface correctness from deeper reconstruction of conventionally-omitted steps, targeting a blind spot that step-level verifiers cannot see since a missing step is not a wrong step.

nodes.label: PRL-Bench dataset (100 open-path physics research tasks)
nodes.norm_label: prl-bench dataset (100 open-path physics research tasks)

nodes.label: QuantumQA Dataset (92,749 hybrid-verified samples)
nodes.rationale: Uses a two-layer verification protocol (symbolic SES + independent LLM critic + human audit) so mathematically fluent but physically wrong responses are caught.

nodes.label: Verification-Aware Reward Model (VRM)
nodes.rationale: Keeps mathematical correctness, physical consistency, and instruction-following as separate reward signals with learned per-instance fusion weighting, because collapsing scientific correctness into one pass/fail signal is too coarse for problems that can be right on some axes and wrong on others.

nodes.label: Distill-then-Classify Chain-of-Thought Error Analysis Pipeline

nodes.label: VerifiableQFT Dataset & Generation Pipeline

nodes.label: Logit-space, bias-decomposed ALS (rank 2)

nodes.label: Observational Scaling Laws (Ruan et al., 2024)
nodes.rationale: Dense-capability-block design fits a denser-data regime than BENCHPRESS's sparse public matrix.

nodes.label: 145-fixture broken-duality benchmark

nodes.label: DualityCert symbolic verifier

nodes.label: Masked feedback control (E5)
nodes.rationale: Isolates whether an agent benefits from semantic content of feedback versus merely its presence/structure, by replacing obligation identities with neutral placeholders.

nodes.label: Sequential intervention target identification
nodes.rationale: Walking backward through the agent chain injecting a hint into one agent at a time turns failure attribution into an agent-level pseudo-label without needing an explicit system-level loss.

nodes.norm_label: recursive-in-recursive self-improvement (inner harness loop + outer rl loop)

nodes.rationale: Authors offer a conjectural small-perturbation Taylor-expansion argument (KL expands to quadratic order in a policy perturbation; if reward is locally linear, reward should scale as sqrt(KL)) as a plausible but unproven explanation for a robust empirical regularity observed across model sizes and PM configurations, explicitly flagged as not fully explained.

nodes.label: Reference-Anchored Discovery Score (RADS)
nodes.rationale: Anchoring 'good' at 50 to mean 'matches the target paper's result' rather than penalizing any deviation from the exact target (punishing valid alternative approaches) or scoring fully open-ended with no anchor (losing evaluability) is a deliberate rubric-design trade-off for scoring open-ended generation against a known-good reference without treating it as the only acceptable answer.

nodes.label: Hypothesis Tree Refinement (HTR)
nodes.rationale: Separates a long-lived coordinator holding durable state (hypothesis+artifact+evidence+insight per node) from short-lived isolated executors, so global strategy survives beyond any single conversation window or executor context limit.

nodes.label: Abstraction Barrier hypothesis
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis (attributed to co-author Lerchner) that systems trained primarily on human-generated data may be unable to discover genuinely novel conceptual primitives from raw reality, illustrated by asking whether a model trained only on pre-Newtonian science could derive general relativity.

nodes.label: Budget-Force Baseline
nodes.rationale: Given a retrospective, oracle-level token-budget advantage unavailable at real deployment time to avoid an easy strawman comparison.

nodes.label: Post-RCP Confirmation Bias / Cognitive Inertia Experiment
nodes.norm_label: post-rcp confirmation bias / cognitive inertia experiment
nodes.rationale: Causal injection of a false intermediate answer shows post-RCP generation mainly rationalizes rather than genuinely re-verifies.

nodes.label: Reasoning Completion Point (RCP)
nodes.rationale: Jointly defined via content-length stabilization and semantic path convergence, marking the point beyond which additional thinking tokens are redundant.

nodes.label: Reasoning Completion Point Detector (RCPD)
nodes.rationale: Distills instance-specific RCP into deterministic online stopping rules based on the rank of the thinking-termination token, avoiding extra computation or fine-tuning.

nodes.label: S-GRPO (training-based early-exit baseline)
nodes.rationale: Compared using numbers taken directly from its original paper, not reproduced under this paper's evaluation setup.

nodes.label: Capability track / behavior track separation
nodes.rationale: Separating what a person knew/did from how they communicated targets a named failure mode of prior persona systems that conflate knowledge, judgment, and tone into one object.

nodes.label: Generalist Computer-Use Agent (GCUA) taxonomy
nodes.rationale: Five functional layers (Brain/Eyes/Body/Hands/Feet) argue CLI-agents and GUI-agents cover genuinely disjoint operational surfaces, not weaker/stronger versions of one capability.

nodes.norm_label: file-level hit vs line-level recall asymmetry

nodes.label: Trajectory-grounded ground-truth construction
nodes.rationale: Derives necessary-context labels from the intersection of multiple independent successful agent trajectories rather than manual annotation, anchoring targets in genuinely observed successful behavior.

nodes.label: Patch-compliance-without-mechanism-fix finding
nodes.rationale: Generated patches close the reported reward expression rather than the underlying exploit mechanism, so surface language adapts while the exploit mechanism persists.

nodes.label: Controlled utility evolution (epoch-boundary evaluator replacement + selective erasure)
nodes.norm_label: controlled utility evolution (epoch-boundary evaluator replacement + selective erasure)
nodes.rationale: Freezing evaluator within an epoch preserves prior Gödel Machine convergence guarantees; selective erasure discards only utility records tied to a displaced evaluator, keeping re-evaluation cost linear via exponential checkpointing.

nodes.label: Red Queen Gödel Machine (RQGM)
nodes.rationale: Lets the evaluator itself be a learned, co-evolving agent rather than a permanently fixed benchmark/verifier, addressing tasks with no direct benchmark or where static judges saturate.

nodes.label: AgingBench benchmark
nodes.rationale: Uses a P1/P2/P3 counterfactual probe ladder to attribute aggregate failure to a specific pipeline stage (write/retrieval/utilization) rather than reporting one memory score.

nodes.rationale: Defined via boundary Table 4 distinguishing episodic environment-action-feedback loops from persistent workspace for task hosting.

nodes.label: Workspace + Skill Thesis
nodes.rationale: Argues persistent workspace plus reusable skill, not a bigger model or more tools alone, turns an LLM into something that can reliably finish real work.

nodes.label: EngramServer (per-user override serving)
nodes.rationale: Swaps in user's small override map, runs forward pass, restores originals to give zero cross-user leakage by construction.

nodes.label: Mini-Engram (178M-1.22B replica models)
nodes.rationale: Trained from scratch because no production Engram-pretrained weights are public.

nodes.label: Engram Architecture (content-addressable sparse memory)

nodes.label: Joint OPT (joint row optimization)

nodes.label: Layered content/skill separation design

nodes.label: Muon optimizer (orthogonalized update)
nodes.rationale: Orthogonalization structurally normalizes update directions independent of coordinate-wise scaling, giving stability at extreme batch sizes where AdamW's element-wise second-moment estimator becomes poorly calibrated.

nodes.label: SOAP slingshot instability (stale preconditioner)
nodes.rationale: Caused by infrequent eigenbasis refresh combined with excluding the current step's gradient; harmless at small scale, catastrophic (divergence) at large batch/model scale.

nodes.label: Update-RMS matching (learning-rate transfer framework)
nodes.rationale: Keeps RMS norm of parameter update consistent across AdamW, SOAP, and Muon to enable a fair comparison rather than confounding results via independent per-optimizer LR tuning; adopted from prior Kimi-Moonshot work.

nodes.label: ACE (Accuracy-Complexity-divErsity) lens

nodes.label: BCIT (gated parameter-update mechanism)
nodes.rationale: Combines source strength and current compatibility multiplicatively (not additively) so strong historical evidence cannot compensate for a poor context match, plus a non-compensable hard-conflict veto to prevent overconfident reuse.

nodes.label: S3Gym: Self-Testing and Self-Judging benchmark

nodes.label: Self-consistency check methodology
nodes.rationale: Requires only the model's own discrete behavior (label or 'unknown'), never internal confidence scores or logits, making it usable on API-only black-box models.

nodes.label: Huang et al. 2023 (ChatGPT self-consistency)
nodes.rationale: Prior attempt failed because ChatGPT's self-reported confidence/importance scores were uncalibrated and it frequently refused to classify with missing information; this paper's discrete-label plus 'unknown' design sidesteps that failure mode.

nodes.label: Lanham et al. 2023 (CoT self-consistency)
nodes.rationale: Reaches a similarly model-and-task-dependent conclusion via a different mechanism (false-fact injection into CoT); authors flag a validity concern that injected facts may look like typos rather than genuinely altering reasoning.

nodes.label: Natural Language Autoencoder (26nla)
nodes.rationale: Structurally different route to the same concern (verbalized self-reports of internal state are not automatically accurate): trains a model to translate internal activations into language, validated via activation-reconstruction accuracy rather than behavioral consistency.

nodes.label: Abacus Embeddings
nodes.rationale: Tags each digit with its position relative to the start of its own number, giving the model an explicit, legible alignment signal that prior positional schemes lacked.

nodes.label: Length Generalization Result (up to 100+ digit addition)

nodes.label: Looped (Recurrent) Transformer Architecture
nodes.rationale: Weight-shared recurrence trained with a progressive loss allocates variable computation to harder problem instances without adding parameters.

nodes.label: Data Contamination Inference (Sec. 4.1)
nodes.rationale: Rests on an informal distributional observation rather than a formal hypothesis test; a subsequent external re-analysis found the null could not be rejected for 21 of 25 models, undercutting the contamination story.

nodes.label: GSM-NoOp (Irrelevant Clause) Test
nodes.rationale: Adds a plausible-sounding but operationally irrelevant clause; the resulting accuracy drop is not repaired even by matched in-context demonstrations of the exact needed skill.

nodes.label: GSM-Symbolic Templated Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Turns fixed benchmark questions into resampleable symbolic templates to expose hidden variance behind a single accuracy number.

nodes.label: Negative cosine temperature schedule (NegCosSch)
nodes.rationale: Starting low then increasing lets the model form coarse separation first before refining within-class compactness; reversing the order (start compact, then sharpen) does not preserve the same benefit per the authors' ablations.

nodes.label: Typicality Bias
nodes.rationale: People systematically prefer familiar, predictable, easy-to-process text over unusual text independent of quality; formalized as log-probability under a reference base model, fitted positively significant on HelpSteer preference pairs.

nodes.label: Verbalized Sampling (VS)
nodes.rationale: Designed to counteract typicality bias in preference data causing mode collapse, by eliciting a probability distribution over candidates rather than a single instance, exploiting annotators' competing preference for representative distributions when a distribution is explicitly requested.

nodes.rationale: Forces short and long loop-count trajectories to agree so stopping early gives coherent output.

nodes.rationale: Borrowed from diffusion models so quality scales smoothly with user-chosen inference compute.

nodes.label: BDH-CQ system
nodes.rationale: Splits recurrent contextual memory (in-context demonstration ingestion) from a separate latent reasoning workspace (iterative query-solving) so no weight updates or verbalized intermediate reasoning are needed at inference time.

nodes.rationale: Instantiates Selective Abstraction at the level of individual atomic claims so a single response can mix fully-specific, partially-abstracted, and abstained content rather than one all-or-nothing decision.

nodes.label: Split Conformal Threshold Calibration
nodes.rationale: Grounded in split conformal prediction to give a formal guarantee that true risk stays within alpha ± epsilon with probability at least 1-delta, avoiding ad hoc threshold picking.

nodes.label: Entity-Narrowing Information Measure
nodes.rationale: Treats a claim as a subject-independent predicate narrowing a reference entity set, giving a comparability across claims not tied to a fixed set of alternative-granularity answers to one question.

nodes.label: Agentic Wikipedia Fact-Checking Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Uses free Wikipedia API instead of paid search API; validated against 102 human-labeled claims (F1 0.93) to justify use as ground-truth oracle.
